'''Amanda Cordelia Bryant-Friedrich''' is the dean of the graduate school and a professor in the college of pharmacy and health sciences at [[Wayne State University]]. She was awarded the 2014 [[American Chemical Society]] Stanley C. Israel Regional Award for Advancing Diversity in the Chemical Sciences and is a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and the [[American Chemical Society]]. Her research considers modified nucleic acids and biomarkers of disease.

== Early life and education ==
Bryant-Friedrich was born in [[Enfield, North Carolina]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-2LULJ6JO_IC&q=Amanda+C.+Bryant-Friedrich+north+carolina&pg=PA3|title=From Oppression to Grace: Women of Color and Their Dilemmas in the Academy|last=Mizelle|first=Nathalie D.|date=2006|publisher=Stylus Publishing, LLC.|isbn=978-1-57922-111-9|language=en}}</ref> She is the daughter of a farmer and, alongside her education in the [[Halifax County Schools (North Carolina)|Halifax County School]] system, worked on the family farm. She graduated high school as [[Valedictorian]] and moved on to attend university.<ref name=":0" /> Whilst she was offered a full academic scholarship at [[Duke University]], she was encouraged by her guidance counsellor to attend North Carolina Central University. She eventually earned her bachelor's degree in chemistry at [[North Carolina Central University]], where she worked in the laboratory of John Meyers.<ref name=":0" /> She became increasingly interested in scientific research and spent a summer holiday as an intern at [[Dow Chemical Company]].<ref name=":0" /> She eventually graduated [[magna cum laude]] with a bachelor's degree in chemistry. She moved to [[Duke University]] for her graduate studies, and spent two years trying to prove to the department that she would be able to complete a PhD. She eventually earned a master's degree in the department of chemistry and began her doctoral research with Richard Polniaszek. Six months after starting, Polniaszek left the university, leaving Byrant-Friedrich to find a new project.<ref name=":0" /> In 1993, after several weeks of German lessons, Byrant-Friedrich moved to [[Heidelberg University]] for her doctoral research. She worked on organic chemistry under the supervision of [[Richard Neidlein]] and completed her PhD in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wilsymposium.com/locations/archives/2018-symposiums/2018-toledo/amanda-bryant-friedrich/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191206221735/http://wilsymposium.com/locations/archives/2018-symposiums/2018-toledo/amanda-bryant-friedrich/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=December 6, 2019|title=Amanda Bryant-Friedrich|website=Women in Leadership Symposium|language=en-US|access-date=2019-12-06}}</ref> Her doctoral research involved the synthesis of complex aromatic compounds.

== Research and career ==
In 1997 Byrant-Friedrich joined the research laboratory of [[Bernd Giese]] at the [[University of Basel]] as a postdoctoral fellow.<ref name=":0" /> Here, she became interested in the use of [[organic chemistry]] as a means to study biological mechanisms.<ref name=":0" /> After spending two years in [[Switzerland]], Byrant-Friedrich moved back to the [[United States]]. Shortly after returning, Bryant-Friedrich worked at [[Wayne State University]], but when it became obvious that she would not be awarded a tenure-track position, she looked for other options.

Byrant-Friedrich joined [[Oakland University]] as an assistant professor in 2000. She was awarded a [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|National Science Foundation CAREER Award]] in 2003, which allowed her to study the chemical processes that damage [[DNA]] and [[RNA]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=0239525|title=NSF Award Search: Award#0239525 - CAREER: C-3'-Nucleic Acid Radicals: Generation and Mechanistic Investigations|website=www.nsf.gov|access-date=2019-12-05}}</ref> She moved to the [[University of Toledo]] in 2007.

Bryant-Friedrich was elected to serve as a 2022 chair in the American Chemical Society Medical Division of Medicinal Chemistry (ACS MEDI).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Aldrich |first1=Jane |last2=Allen |first2=Shelley |last3=Araujo |first3=Erika |last4=Bronson |first4=Joanne |last5=Bryant-Friedrich |first5=Amanda |last6=Cyr |first6=Shana K. |last7=DiMauro |first7=Erin F. |last8=Dzierba |first8=Carolyn |last9=Garner |first9=Amanda L. |last10=Georg |first10=Gunda I. |last11=Goodwin |first11=Nicole C. |last12=Haranahalli |first12=Krupanandan |last13=Huang |first13=Rong |last14=Leftheris |first14=Katerina |last15=May-Dracka |first15=Tricia L. |date=2023-03-08 |title=Enhancing the Visibility of Women in the ACS Division of Medicinal Chemistry (ACS MEDI) |journal=ACS Medicinal Chemistry Letters |volume=14 |issue=4 |language=en |pages=345–349 |doi=10.1021/acsmedchemlett.3c00069 |issn=1948-5875|doi-access=free |pmid=37077389 |pmc=10107900 }}</ref>

She studies the mechanisms by which small molecules interact with [[nucleic acid]]. Her research involves the synthesis of modified [[Nucleoside|nucleosides]] and nucleotides, monitoring the intercalation of small aromatic systems into [[DNA]] ''via'' the design of novel [[Chromophore|chromophores]] and the creation of probes that contain nucleic acids to study events that occur around [[DNA]]. She has studied the protection of [[small nuclear RNA]] (snRNAs) from [[oxidative damage]], which typically damages cells.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1904754&HistoricalAwards=false|title=NSF Award Search: Award#1904754 - Creation of tools to determine the impact of natural modifications on RNA damage|website=www.nsf.gov|access-date=2019-12-05}}</ref> As [[snRNA]] is essential for the function of [[spliceosome]], this type of damage can impact the structure and function of the [[spliceosome]].

=== Academic service ===
In 2016 it was announced that Byrant-Friedrich would become the dean of the college of graduate studies at the [[University of Toledo]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.toledoblade.com/local/education/2016/06/01/New-dean-named-for-University-of-Toledo-grad-studies-program/stories/20160531287|title=Dean named for UT graduate studies|website=Toledo Blade|language=en|access-date=2019-12-05}}</ref> She holds various honorary positions, including commissioner for the [[Lake Erie]] Commission. She has simultaneously held leadership roles in the [[American Chemical Society]] Division of Toxicology and Medicinal Chemistry.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=L75mDwAAQBAJ&q=University+of+Toledo+University+Women%E2%80%99s+Commission+amanda.+bryant&pg=PA94|title=Mom the Chemistry Professor: Personal Accounts and Advice from Chemistry Professors who are Mothers|last1=Woznack|first1=Kimberly|last2=Charlebois|first2=Amber|last3=Cole|first3=Renée|last4=Marzabadi|first4=Cecilia|last5=Webster|first5=Gail|date=2018-07-28|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-3-319-78972-9|language=en}}</ref> Alongside her research and administrative duties, Byrant-Friedrich works to support women and minority scientists.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=If7IBAAAQBAJ&q=University+of+Toledo+University+Women%E2%80%99s+Commission+amanda.+bryant&pg=PA91|title=FORWARD to Professorship in STEM: Inclusive Faculty Development Strategies That Work|last1=Heller|first1=Rachelle S.|last2=Mavriplis|first2=Catherine|author2-link=Catherine Mavriplis|last3=Sabila|first3=Paul S.|date=2015-12-07|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=978-0-12-801128-7|language=en}}</ref>

In 2020, Bryant-Friedrich was named the dean of the graduate school at [[Wayne State University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://today.wayne.edu/news/2020/05/27/amanda-bryant-friedrich-named-dean-of-the-graduate-school-37400|title=Amanda Bryant-Friedrich named dean of the Graduate School|website=Today@Wayne|date=15 May 2018 |language=en|access-date=2020-08-06}}</ref> Additionally, she was hired to teach at Wayne State's College of Pharmacy and Health Sciences, where she would run a laboratory to conduct research.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gradschool.wayne.edu/news/qa-with-amanda-bryant-friedrich-new-dean-of-the-graduate-school-40281|title=Q&A with Amanda Bryant-Friedrich, new dean of the Graduate School|website=Wayne State University Graduate School|language=en|access-date=2020-08-06}}</ref>

=== Awards and honours ===
Her awards and honours include:

* 2015 [[University of Toledo]] University Women's Commission
* 2018 Elected a Fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/fellows/list-of-2018-acs-fellows.html|title=2018 ACS Fellows|website=American Chemical Society|language=en|access-date=2019-12-05}}</ref>
* 2019 [[Girl Scouts of the USA|Girl Scouts]] of Western Ohio Women of Distinction<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gswo.org/en/donate/women-of-distinction/toledo.html|title=Women of Distinction - Toledo|website=Girl Scouts|language=en|access-date=2019-12-05}}</ref>
* 2019 Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/page/2019-fellows|title=2019 Fellows|website=American Association for the Advancement of Science|language=en|access-date=2019-12-05}}</ref>
*2020 [[YWCA]] Northwest Ohio Milestone Award for science<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news.utoledo.edu/index.php/12_05_2019/president-dean-named-ywca-milestone-honorees|title=UToledo News » Blog Archive » President, Dean Named YWCA Milestone Honorees|website=news.utoledo.edu|date=5 December 2019 |access-date=2019-12-06}}</ref>

=== Personal life ===
Byrant-Friedrich was profiled in {{Cite book|title=African American Women Chemists in the Modern Era|last=|date=8 August 2018|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=9780190615185|location=|pages=}} She is married to Klaus Friedrich with whom she has two children.<ref name=":1" />
